title: third-party-scan-collab-checklist-and-evidence-flow
body:
Purpose
This doc is a working coordination checklist and evidence packaging runbook for third-party security scans focused on RBAC v2, audit-log schema verification, SIEM export checks, and automated evidence delivery. Intended audience: security ops, infra, SRE, platform, and the external assessor team.

High-level goals
- Ensure assessor has clear scope boundaries and access methods.
- Provide reproducible evidence artifacts (logs, screenshots, export files) that map to assessment requirements.
- Automate the bulk of evidence collection to minimize manual handoff and preserve chain-of-custody.

Stakeholders and roles
- Owner: Aisha Kumaran (secops) — overall coordination, communications.
- Infra lead: Diego Morales — log exports, identity, and network access.
- Platform eng: Hannah Lee — RBAC v2 feature walkthrough and smoke tests.
- SRE: Rory Patel — KMS/TLS and runtime evidence, bucket access.
- Product security reviewer: Maya Thompson — approves redaction and release of artifacts.
- External assessor: third-party vendor (named in onboarding doc).

Pre-engagement checklist (2 weeks before)
- Confirm scope doc and data sensitivity matrix with legal/product. Link: CONFLUENCE-ONBOARD.
- Create ephemeral assessment account(s) with least privilege matching scope. Tag accounts: assessment/scan-YYYYMMDD.
- Freeze changes to RBAC config and logging pipeline during active scan window.
- Confirm retention windows: ensure logs for last 90 days available (or scope-defined).
- Prepare an artifacts S3/GCS bucket with 3-day TTL and access logs enabled.
- Generate service account for assessor and populate in allowlist for IPs.

RBAC v2 test mapping (what to provide)
- Provide RBAC model diagram (roles, permissions, inheritance) as PDF.
- Export role assignments CSV (fields: principal_type, principal_id, role_id, resource_pattern, assignment_date).
- Provide sample API calls (curl + API key) demonstrating allowed and denied responses. Include request/response bodies and timestamps.
- Run systematic permission enumeration script (scripts/perm-enum.sh) that logs attempts and captures audit record ids. Include output CSV.

Audit log schema verification (expected fields and examples)
- Provide sample event lines (raw JSON) with required fields: timestamp, event_id, actor_id, actor_type, resource, action, outcome (success|failure), request_id, trace_id, user_agent, ip, region, kv_pairs (freeform)
- Map schema fields to SIEM fields and Elastic/Cloud index names. Provide a mapping table file (audit-schema-mapping.csv).
- Identify any internal-only fields that must be redacted prior to sharing (e.g., internal_trace_blob).

SIEM export and validation steps
- Verify continuous export pipeline: log producer -> ingestion layer -> SIEM index -> export snapshot.
- Run export smoke test: create synthetic event with marker string "scan-evidence-<timestamp>" and confirm exported file includes it. Save result file with name pattern evidence-snapshot-<date>.ndjson.gz.
- Validate field parity: run a query against the exported NDJSON to assert presence of required fields (simple jq script included).

Evidence automation runbook (high level)
- Trigger: manual or scheduled job in CI (github action: .github/workflows/evidence-export.yml).
- Steps:
  1) Create ephemeral folder in artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-sec-evidence/<scan-id>/
  2) Pull index snapshot from SIEM retention (API call) for time window -> write ndjson.gz
  3) Run schema-normalizer script to add standardized columns (event_id, canonical_action, resource_scope)
  4) Redact sensitive fields using allowlist (run redaction tool with config redaction/allowlist.yml)
  5) Compute checksums (sha256) for each artifact and write manifest.jsonl with checksum, filename, size, generated_at
  6) Put manifest and artifacts in bucket, enable signed URL for assessor with 7-day expiry
  7) Notify stakeholders and post Jira SEC ticket comment with artifact URLs

Minimal artifact list to produce
- rbacs-export.csv (role assignments)
- rbacs-diagram.pdf (SVG->PDF)
- audit-snapshot-<date>.ndjson.gz (logs for window)
- export-manifest.jsonl (checksums + metadata)
- smoke-test-request-response.log (curl traces for API smoke tests)
- siem-export-validation.txt (results of automated checks)

Chain-of-custody and redaction notes
- Everything in artifacts bucket must be write-once where possible. Use object lock or retention policy for 72h.
- Redaction rules: do not share user PII (email, full IP), do not expose internal secret ids or trace blobs. Product security must review before sharing.

Common assessor requests and responses (fast templates)
- Q: Can we access an admin console to run queries?
  A: No interactive console; we provide curated exports and scriptable APIs. If interactive access is needed, provide timeboxed bastion session and session recording.
- Q: Can you re-run a scenario to produce reproducible logs?
  A: Yes — use test account scan-user-xxx and steps in reproducibility.md.

Timeline and milestones
- Week -2: Confirm scope, service accounts created, artifact bucket ready
- Week -1: Smoke tests and RBAC exports validated
- Assessment week: run exports daily, automate manifest updates, sync with assessor daily stand
- Post-assessment (D+1 to D+5): deliver final evidence pack and remediation tracker

Post-scan remediation tracking
- Create consolidated findings spreadsheet (columns: id, title, severity, finding_summary, repro_steps, raw_artifact_refs, owner, due_date, status).
- Assign owners and schedule remediation demo.
- For RBAC issues, attach changed role diff and timestamped commit/PR id.

Notes / open questions (TO DO)
- Confirm whether network flow logs (VPC flow) are in scope for external assessor — if yes, include mapping and sample export.
- Decide on maximum allowed redaction level (full IP vs truncated). Product security to decide by 2026-02-27.
- Add automated attestation step where product sec signs manifest using KMS key and publishes signature alongside manifest.

Appendix: quick commands
- Generate role export (example): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" "https://api.redwood/v1/roles/export?format=csv" -o rbacs-export.csv
- Create smoke event: curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/events -d '{"marker":"scan-evidence-20260220","msg":"test"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
- Validate ndjson fields: zcat audit-snapshot-20260220.ndjson.gz | head -n 20 | jq -c '. | {timestamp,event_id,actor_id,action,outcome,trace_id}'

Notes to self: keep this doc iterative. Capture assessor feedback in the Confluence onboarding page and consolidate automation improvements into infra repo (GH-issue infra/log-export-312).
